newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian sues to revoke national anthem.
newsitem.headline: Colombian sues to revoke national anthem.

text.p: A Colombian has filed a lawsuit with the Constitutional Court seeking to revoke the national anthem on the grounds that it promotes Catholicism, violence and sadomasochism, it was reported on Monday.

Bogota's El Espectador newspaper said the suit was filed last Friday by Alexandre Sochandamadou, who won decriminalization of the individual use of small quantities of illicit drugs through a suit filed with the court in 1994.
In his latest action, Sochandamadou is targeting lyrics of the national anthem penned over a century ago by former president Rafael Nunez, the newspaper said.

Among other objectionable stanzas, according to Sochandamadou, is a line referring to "good sprouting from furrows of suffering," which he says represents an apology for violence and sadomasochism since it teaches that good comes from pain.

His lawsuit argues that other stanzas could be seen as encouraging leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups, and the country's high levels of violence, because they urge all good Colombians to take up arms to defend the truth.

Sochandamadou argues that the anthem contradicts the official separation between the Roman Catholic church and the state since it is sung at all government ceremonies and encourages Colombians to follow "the words of he who died on the cross."

El Espectador said Constitutional Court magistrate Vladimiro Naranjo would decide within the next few days whether there were sufficient grounds for the court to determine whether the anthem violates Colombia's national charter.
